question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}5x+2y=1 \\ \frac{2x}{3}-\frac{y}{9}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.

$x=$
{{field-1}}$,\,y=$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the second equation, we must multiply the second equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $9.$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5x+2y=1 \\ \frac{2x}{3}-\frac{y}{9}=-1 & |\,\times 9\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}5x+2y=1 \\ 6x-y=-9\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Let's solve for $y$ in the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}6x-y & =-9 \\ 6x+9 & =y \\ y & =6x+9\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute $y=6x+9$ into the first equation and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+2y & =1 \\ 5x+2(6x+9) & =1 \\ 5x+12x+18 & =1 \\ 17x+18 & =1 \\ 17x & =-17 \\ x & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $y,$ we substitute $x=-1$ into the equation $y=6x+9,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =6x+9 \\  & =6(-1)+9 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-1,\,y=3.$
